question: Should OpenClaw core own this publisher-feed trust and transport boundary now, and if so which production caller and canonical trust-root source must land with it?
rationale: Accepting remote signed publisher projections establishes a new client trust boundary, but the draft currently supplies only injectable primitives while the RFC, producers, trust-key rollout, and product integration remain open.

options.title: Land A Coordinated Vertical Slice
options.body: Require the approved RFC and producer contract, a production OpenClaw caller with canonical trust-key ownership, and live query/change/reset proof in the same landing sequence.

options.title: Keep The Stack Draft
options.body: Leave this PR open as a draft until the dependency and producer PRs settle, then refresh it against the final contract.

options.title: Move The Consumer Boundary
options.body: If no core product path owns publisher feeds, place the service-specific client in an appropriate plugin or ClawHub-owned package and expose only genuinely missing generic seams from core.

recommendation.title: Land A Coordinated Vertical Slice
recommendation.body: Require the approved RFC and producer contract, a production OpenClaw caller with canonical trust-key ownership, and live query/change/reset proof in the same landing sequence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged feed-contract and plugin-catalog history most directly spans the producer contract and OpenClaw catalog ownership involved in this decision.
